chapter: Leaving Hampton and starting his own band
title: The Baby Grand Cafe on April 29 and his first record contract
summary: Cobb's group fills in for Billie Holiday at Harlem's Baby Grand, nearly gets fired for being loud, is kept, and gets a recording contract with Apollo.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: The very first job they booked me on -- no, I won't say that, not the very first -- while I'm in the office, get a call from Baby Grand Cafe on 125th. Billie Holiday had received a $75.00 deposit to play 29th and the 30th of April. And she was in Chicago working, and they needed a group in there.

So Ralph said, "We got it. He's right here now, Arnett Cobb." They said, "Good." They had never had anything in there above a trio. I happen to remember the date so well. It's my anniversary date of me and this gal here, our eighth anniversary, 29th of April. We were married the 29th of April, 1939.

I went in there. A friend of mine had hit the numbers that day. He bought a party in there, spent about $150.00, $160.00, stayed in that two days, from the two days -- I got two weeks after that from it. But the main thing that happened in there was that the guy, Bill Potter, who was the manager of the club, said the band was too loud, because I had two horns, just me and the trumpet player.

Then I started to walking around on "Flying Home" and all this, and he didn't like that. And I played (inaudible) Lionel Hampton -- okay (inaudible). And the man that owned the joint found out what the cash register said. He told him, said, "Let him alone." I stayed there two more weeks.
And in there I got my first recording contract for Apollo Parlor Records. And things just went on from that point on.
